text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's Prime minister Zhan Videnov said he would personally negotiate the transit of Russian natural gas through Bulgaria and not the president of the private business grouping Multigroup Ilia Pavlov, in a bid to protect the national interests. @

-- Former economic advisor to Zhan Videnov Ivan Angelov said the cabinet should ban domestic foreign exchange trading this week to prevent a new slump in the lev and urgently peg the lev to the German mark at an appropriate exchange rate.

-- Bulgaria's Mass Privatisation Centre (MPC) is expected to announce today results of the first voucher privatisation tender, in which 81 privatisation funds and 392,000 individuals bid for shares of 986 state companies with total assets of 77.164 billion levs, a MPC senior official said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet planned an exchange rate of 830 levs per dollar in a draft budget for 1997 assuming a currency board system was not introduced in the country, the newspaper said without quoting sources.

-- Bulgaria's National Insurance Institute (NII) should have a reserve of some 35 billion levs to gurantee pension payments if a currency board system was introduced in the country, a NII senior official said.

-- The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank might extend $1.6 billion to Bulgaria to support the introduction of a currency board system provided a large scale structural reform was implemented, the newspaper said quoting an unnamed source, who was not a native Bulgarian speaker.
-- Bulgaria's police seized on Sunday eight containers with radioactive cesium 137, plutonium and uranium in the northeastern village of Golyam Porovets, the Interior ministry said. @

-- Bulgaria's biggest state refinery Neftochim would not reduce fuel sales to local retailers by the end of the year despite big losses from the fall in the lev, Neftochim officials said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
